Alloy ingots with a nominal composition of Co40Ni30Cr20Al5Ti5 (a.t. %) were fabricated using a vacuum suspension melting furnace under a high-purity argon atmosphere. To ensure compositional homogeneity, each ingot was remelted at least five times and cast into water-cooled copper molds (50 mm diameter, 45 mm height).
The cast ingots were sectioned into thin sheets with a thickness of 4.5 mm and homogenized at 1150 ◦C for 2 h to eliminate elemental segregation during solidification.
Subsequently, the homogenized sheets were cold-rolled to a total thickness reduction of 65 % through multiple passes, with a reduction of 5–10 % per pass.
The deformed sheets underwent static recrystallization at 1150 ◦C for 2 min, followed by aging at 800 ◦C for 4 h to promote precipitation.

Thermal stability of the Co40Ni30Cr20Al5Ti5 alloy was evaluated after prolonged aging at 800 ◦C for 240 h, employing comprehensive microstructural analyses.
XRD analysis ( Fig. 2 a) confirmed a dual-phase structure comprising face-centered cubic (FCC) and L12 phases.
In-depth compositional analysis confirmed that Ni, Al, and Ti were enriched in the L12 nanoprecipitates, while Co and Cr were predominantly segregated within the FCC matrix ( Fig. 5 a).

This phenomenon is primarily attributed to the Zener pinning effect [ 23 ] exerted by stable L12 nanoprecipitates, which impede boundary motion and stabilize the microstructure ( Fig. S1 ).
This shift indicates a transition from dislocation-driven deformation to grain boundary-mediated mechanisms, such as grain boundary sliding, as evidenced by intergranular fracture ( Fig. 8 d).

The ductile-to-brittle transition at 800 ◦C is driven by thermally activated dislocation mobility and rapid dynamic recovery, which reduce the work hardening rate and cause fracture at reduced stress levels.

In FCC-structured MPEAs, coherent L12-type multicomponent intermetallic nanoprecipitates promote multistage work-hardening by enhancing dislocation storage capacity and facilitating the formation of deformation-induced microbands.
